Method of Attack: Sending an email containing a zipped .URL shortcut file that opens a remote script file which downloads and executes a final payload
Using .URL Windows shortcut files disguised with folder icons to trick users into launching the infection chain
Simplified infection chain relying on zipped .URL files to evade email malware scanners
Attack Vector: Email attachments containing zipped .URL shortcut files
Indicators of Compromise: Email attachments with zipped .URL files showing the classic Windows shortcut arrow icon on the bottom-left corner
Use of standard folder icon to disguise .URL files in email attachments
